overview: Two of the extra-embryonic membranes that protect and support the developing embryo, with different structural roles.
genZNote: Chorion: the outer membrane that helps build the placenta. Amnion: the inner water balloon cushioning the baby.

aspects.label: Position
aspects.valueB: The innermost membrane, directly surrounding the embryo/fetus.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Forms the fetal part of the placenta and contributes to gas/nutrient exchange with the mother.
aspects.valueB: Encloses the amniotic fluid, cushioning and protecting the embryo from mechanical shock.

aspects.label: Associated Fluid
aspects.valueB: Encloses the amniotic cavity, filled with amniotic fluid.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Amniotic fluid sampling (amniocentesis) is a prenatal diagnostic technique that draws directly from the amnion's fluid-filled cavity.
overlay.memoryTrick: Chorion contributes to the placenta (outer). Amnion holds the fluid cushion (inner).
overlay.commonMisconception: The chorion and amnion are not the same membrane at different times — they are two distinct, simultaneously present extra-embryonic membranes.
